fieldValues.title: Review: is the decision checklist helping the owner judge?
fieldValues.thinking_reached: First version written 2026-11-05 from the owner's meeting review, the muDemocracy guide, the handbook's four tests and srs#998. DC-01 to DC-11 follow the meeting's checklist; DC-12 to DC-14 are additions from srs#998 and have not been tried. DC-15 (consequences in the decision's own context) was added the same day on the owner's words (vignettes 8b9cb702 and 2f33caa2), after a hand-written version of it on srs#998 D1 proved far more valuable for review. This exercise stays open and on every owner session's agenda until three reviews in a row change nothing.
fieldValues.tensions:
Thorough against light: every check added is a cost on each decision, and DC-11 must keep small decisions small.
Mechanical against judgement: a check a tool can pass can be filled to pass (9b9f9434: form 97%, substance 41%).
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: At each session: Which decision was hardest to judge, and what was missing? Which check did you actually use? Which did nothing? Did you change or refuse a recommendation, and did a check prompt it? Were the strategic paths stated in DC-15 the real ones? Record the answers as comments here, with any check changed.
fieldValues.next_action: Review at the next owner session. On srs#998 the owner answered D1 and D2 and found the strategic table more valuable than the rewritten block alone; the RFC itself is still a Draft, not accepted. Next test: the next technical decision to reach the owner.
